## 8. DO NOT do this in a Software Engineering Interview
**Channel:** CodingWithMitch | **Views:** 10K | **Date:** 3 years ago | **Duration:** 7:59 | **ID:** sJ0ifNkRj0o

in this video I'm going to show you four things that you absolutely should not be doing in your software engineering interviews these are more behavioral things they're not necessarily like you know solving the problem or getting the correct solution sort of thing these are more behavioral things that stick out to me that tell me do I want to work with this person and really when you think about it whether or not the interviewer wants to work with you is a huge part of the interview it's probably at least 50 percent whether or not you are a pleasant person to be around a pleasant person to talk to you accept feedback in a positive way these are huge indicators and they can make or break your interview number one when the interviewer suggests an alternative to the pathway that you've chosen to solve a certain problem what do you do in that scenario I think there's a there's a there's a couple ways you can respond to this and there's only really one good way the first not good way is you take with you okay so suppose you are in implementing we'll we'll say path a and path B suppose you've chosen path a to implement Your solution and the interviewer suggests an alternative path we'll call it path B the first way that you could respond to this which is not a good way is you could just take what they say and just do it don't really say anything just say oh okay I'll do it that way that doesn't really tell the interview or anything what they're looking for here is they're looking to see that you you think about the pathway that you chose and you think about the pathway that they've suggested you and you you take them in and you decide which one is the best because they might not necessarily be suggesting a better way they might be suggesting an inferior way but they want you to say okay I'm going down path a you've suggested path B what would path B look like and then you look at both of them and you and you say okay if I do path a it's gonna this is what's gonna happen if I do path B this is what's going to happen and they want to see you choose the the better response the other other incorrect way to respond to this problem is to brush off what they say if if an interviewer I think there's only two reasons that an interviewer would would suggest something they they want to suggest a inferior solution and they want to see you come to the correct one they want to see okay you've chosen path a which is the best one they're they're going to suggest a less efficient route and they want to see you think that through and say okay that's less efficient I'm going to go with the one that I originally started with or you're going the less efficient route and they're trying to help you they're trying to say hey pal like that's not the right way but they they don't want to tell you that they want you to take in their suggestion again weigh them both out and figure out which path is the best one so if an interviewer gives you some kind of feedback some kind of suggestion those are typically the two reasons the best response is the same in both scenarios you want to take your path their path compare them talk about them and choose the right one number two is referencing docu documentation a lot of people get kind of weird about referencing documentation while some people do some people don't you should think when if suppose you're doing a problem and you get stuck and you gotta pull up some documentation because you don't you don't remember you don't memorize everything you should consider this a gift this is a great thing in an interviewer if you get the chance to pull up documentation and Implement something you know you should almost go as far as to faking that you don't know something so that you can pull up documentation that's how I feel that's how strongly I feel about this because so much of a software engineer's job is pulling up documentation reading documents that people have written and going through them and implementing what they say if you get stuck or fake that you get stuck and you pull up documentation you follow the documentation and you successfully implement it this is a beautiful thing this is something that we're all looking for in interviews we want to see that there's a thing that you're unable to do you pull up some kind of information and you solve the problem this is great you should should not be scared of this you should not try to not bring up documentation if anything you should try and fake somehow a scenario where you need to bring up documentation number three if you get stuck or you don't know what you're doing don't pretend like you're not stuck or don't pretend like you do know what you're doing I saw this in an interview recently and it was so bad me and the interviewer helped this guy so many times he got stuck so many times every time we suggested something he either brushed off our suggestions as if it was nothing or he took what we suggested implemented it and then was like oh okay yeah I guess you could do it that way and that was his tone that was the way he said it don't do this if you're stuck say you're stuck or ask the interviewer hey what would you do here and they'll help you they'll give you a suggestion this is another thing that is telling us do we want to work with this person because everybody gets stuck I get stuck on something most days like you're always talking to each other whether on video You're pairing or or you're on slack whatever like it's gonna happen basically just don't like if someone's helping you don't act like they didn't help you acknowledge it say thank you and and move on don't just try and pretend like oh I I would have got the answer if you know eventually or oh yeah I was going to do that next or whatever like just acknowledge it it's not a problem like they're looking to see that you're able that you're not somebody terrible to work with number four this one is a true killer this one is more about optimizing your time and it's very common to run out of time on these interviews so if you are let's suppose you are trying to implement a solution and this solution has 10 total steps usually when you're trying to figure something out you it's not clear how many steps there's gonna be but let's just for the sake of being um some being practical let's say there's 10 steps don't try and optimize your solution at step one two three four five try to get to a working solution and then go back and optimize it now the other side of this coin is it's kind of a gray area like obviously you should be optimizing throughout your solution as best you can but all I'm saying is don't get hung up on optimizing it's much better to have a working solution that is not you know maximum performance then have then get to like step five out of ten and be the most performant thing ever so you got to kind of do a balancing act here if you can optimize as you go obviously that's ideal but don't waste time try to get to that working solution and then go back and say okay how can I make this faster how can I make this more readable things like that even as the interviewer say hey like I got a solution like hmm I feel like you know this section could be better like do you have any suggestions most interviewers will work with you and try to come to a solution because that's
